text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Governments of Bosnia's Serb and Moslem-Croat entities fail to sign an agreement on inter-entity trade cooperation after meeting in Pale.
- Hasan Cengic, former Moslem-Croat federation defence minister, denies speculation that eastern town of Gorazde might be exchanged for northwestern territory in the Serb entity.
- Cengic said that via Gorazde, Bosnian refugees will eventually return to towns in Serb territory such as Foca, Zvornik, Bijeljina and Srebrenica.
- Russian envoy Igor Ivanov says during visit to Sarajevo that Russia is ready to offer favorable credits for reconstruction projects after laws on economic reforms are adopted.

- Representatives of four religious communities in Bosnia, met in Mostar for the first time since war erupted in 1992. They appealled for religious tolerance among Moslems, Roman Catholics, Orthodox Christians and Jews.

- Ministry of foreign affairs propose appointment of 29 new ambassadors, deputy foreign minister Husein Zivalj says. The appointments followed warning from High Representative Carl Bildt, that he would ask the international community not to recognise any ambassadors if they were not approved by the collective presidency by July 1997.
- The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia's Internet page shows a map in which Yugoslavia borders the Serb entity and the Moslem-Croat federation but Bosnia is not mentioned at all, newspaper says.

- McDonald's may open a restaurant in Sarajevo, newspaper says. Negotiations are under way between McDonald's and an investor from Kuwait, which is currently remodelling an old restaurant damaged during the war.
- Opposition shadow government appeals to international community to step up efforts to establish functioning joint institutions and create conditions for Bosnia's economic revival.
- Trade Union Association protests over an attack orchestrated by Croat police against Bosnian rail workers on May 14 near the border with Croatia. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864
